title: SMD# 26-006, Optional Hold Harmless Period for Community Engagement Implementation (State Medicaid Director letter)
short: Federal letter to state Medicaid directors, Nov. 13, 2026 (SMD# 26-006)
public_note: Read in full on 2026-11-14: 4 pages, 3 footnotes, signed by Daniel Brillman, Deputy Administrator and Director. Offers every state an optional hold harmless period through June 30, 2027. A state that elects it may suspend denials of eligibility and disenrollments when an applicable individual does not demonstrate compliance with community engagement. This covers applications received and renewals initiated through and including June 30, 2027. A state may implement a shorter period. A state may use the period only if it assesses whether each individual meets the requirement (including deemed compliance) or is excluded, for all relevant applications and renewals in the period. The period covers only conditioning eligibility on community engagement (section 1902(xx)(1) of the Act, 42 C.F.R. 435.559); it does not apply to any other part of implementing community engagement by Jan. 1, 2027, or to denials and disenrollments on other eligibility criteria, such as age or household income. A state requests the period in its mitigation plan and must have CMS approval before using it; a state that intends to use it from Jan. 1, 2027 is asked to notify CMS by Dec. 11, 2026. For applications submitted and renewals initiated after the period ends in a state, the state must deny or terminate eligibility for not meeting the requirement, after the noncompliance procedures at 42 C.F.R. 435.558. The letter does not name any state that has elected the period. Terms: the letter calls the requirement 'community engagement' and says CMS refers to Public Law No. 119-21 as the 'Working Families Tax Cut' (WFTC) legislation. Footnote 3 cites Massachusetts v. Oz as No. 26-12692-RGS; the order in this registry (S28) carries No. 1:26-cv-12962. medicaid.gov answered 403 to a plain automated request on 2026-11-14; the PDF was fetched with a web fetch tool and its text extracted with pdftotext. The CMS press release of the same day is not registered: the letter is the primary source and no page links to the release.

title: Submit my verification

Key points: after an application or renewal, a letter may ask for more information (a Post Eligibility Review, or PER); HCA staff confirm eligibility based on income, citizenship, or lawful presence. A person has 15 days from the date the letter was mailed, and may ask for more time by email or at 1-800-562-3022. A person must answer even if they just updated their information. Coverage may close if they do not. Documents can be uploaded in the Healthplanfinder document center, emailed, faxed to 1-855-867-4467, or mailed. The read confirms claims WA-APP-09, WA-LTR-02, WA-WRD-05, and WA-LOG-03.

title: WAC 182-505-0250, Washington apple health: MAGI-based adult medical
date_on_document: Two versions shown: effective until January 1, 2027 (filed July 29, 2014), and effective January 1, 2027 (WSR 26-19-026, filed September 8, 2026)
public_note: Read in full on 2026-11-13 on the Legislature's site, both versions shown there. Both say: age 19 or older and under 65. Not entitled to or enrolled in Medicare Part A or B. Not eligible for certain mandatory coverage. Meets the citizenship and immigration rule (WAC 182-503-0535) and the general eligibility rule (WAC 182-503-0505). Net countable income at or below 133 percent of the federal poverty level. The section does not use the figure 138 percent that HCA's fact sheet (WA05) uses, and it reaches residency only through the general eligibility rule. The version effective January 1, 2027 adds a 6-month certification period, 12 months for American Indians and Alaska Natives. The registry title was corrected to the rule's own caption on 2026-11-13. The caption has a dash where the title has a colon. The read confirms claim WA-WRD-02. It does not confirm the 138 percent figure in claim WA-CHK-01 as written.

title: WAC 182-504-0035, Washington apple health: Renewals
date_on_document: Two versions shown: effective September 6, 2025 until January 1, 2027, and effective January 1, 2027 (WSR 26-19-026, filed September 8, 2026)
public_note: Read in full on 2026-11-13 on the Legislature's site, both versions shown there. Subsection (2)(b), for MAGI programs, until January 1, 2027: "you have 90 days from the termination date to give us a completed renewal. If we decide you are still eligible to get apple health coverage, we will restore your apple health without a gap in coverage." The same subsection effective January 1, 2027: "you have 90 days from the termination date to give us a completed renewal without requiring a new application." The sentence on restoring coverage without a gap is not in the 2027 version for MAGI programs. Both versions say the agency reconsiders without a new application in two cases. One: it gets the needed information within 30 days of the date on the termination notice. Two: a hearing is requested within 90 days of the date on the renewal denial letter, and a judge finds the decision wrong. The 2027 version adds renewals every six months for Apple Health for Adults, every 12 months for American Indians and Alaska Natives. The registry title was corrected to the rule's own caption on 2026-11-13. Claim WA-DEN-01 and the page text it feeds were corrected on 2026-11-13 to match both versions.

title: WAC 182-504-0130, Washington apple health: Continued coverage pending an appeal
public_note: Read in full on 2026-11-13 on the Legislature's site. To qualify for continued coverage, a person must request a hearing by one of two deadlines. The first is the tenth day after the agency sent the notice. The second is the last day of the month before the action takes effect. A deadline that falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or designated holiday extends to 5:00 p.m. the next business day. Subsection (5) sets an exception no guide page states. A person cannot receive continued coverage if the action was due solely to a change in statute, federal regulation, or administrative rule. The exception lifts if there is a question about whether the person is in the class of people affected by the change. The registry title was corrected to the rule's own caption on 2026-11-13. The read confirms claim WA-DEN-04.

title: WAC 182-526-0200, Enrollee appeals of a managed care organization action
public_note: Read in full on 2026-11-13 on the Legislature's site. An enrollee must exhaust the managed care organization's grievance and appeal process before requesting a hearing. The hearing must be requested within 120 calendar days of the date of receipt of the organization's notice of resolution. To keep services going during the hearing, the request must be made within ten days of the date of that notice. Applies when the decision being challenged was made by a managed care organization rather than by HCA. The registry title was corrected to the rule's own caption on 2026-11-13. The read confirms claim WA-DEN-03; the rule counts the 120 days from receipt of the notice.

title: WAC 182-503-0080, Washington apple health: Application denials and withdrawals
public_note: Read in full on 2026-11-13 on the Legislature's site. The 90 days appears in subsection (4)(c). The agency reconsiders a denial without a new application when the person requests a hearing within ninety days of the date on the denial letter. An administrative law judge or HCA review judge must decide the denial was wrong. Subsection (5) says a person who disagrees can ask for a hearing. The registry title was corrected to the rule's own caption on 2026-11-13. The read confirms claim WA-DEN-05; the 90 days run from the date on the denial letter.

It lists other coverage to check: Apple Health for Kids, Apple Health for pregnant individuals, After-Pregnancy Coverage, Alien Emergency Medical, Medical Care Services, and Family Planning Only. The page itself does not say the program is state-funded and does not show a December 2025 date. Its privacy section lists Apple Health Expansion among "Apple Health programs that get federal funding". Those two points are on the linked announcement ("Apple Health Expansion enrollment cap", dated Feb. 20, 2026, with an update headed December 2025, which says enrollment is closed and that the budget proposal continues state funds for the program). The announcement was read on 2026-11-13 and is not in this registry. The read confirms that enrollment is closed; it does not confirm claim WA-IMM-04 as written.
